lyrics:
[Intro: one pounding sequencer riff, live drums crash in]

[Verse 1: shouted male voice, German]
Steh auf, steh auf
Mach das Licht an
Beweg die Füße
Und tanz den Montag

[Chorus: riff and drums, gang shout]
Tanz den Montag!
Tanz den Kalender!
Tanz den Wecker!
Und klatsch in die Hände!

[Verse 2: shouted, drums harder]
Dreh dich nach links
Dreh dich nach rechts
Tanz die Deadline
Tanz den Rest

[Chorus: riff and drums, gang shout]
Tanz den Montag!
Tanz den Kalender!
Tanz den Wecker!
Und klatsch in die Hände!

[Break: drums only, whispered]
Montag. Dienstag. Mittwoch.
Donnerstag. Freitag.

[Final Chorus: fastest feel, everyone]
Tanz den Montag!
Tanz den Kalender!
Tanz den Freitag!
Und geh nach Hause!

[Outro: riff stops, one drum hit, an alarm clock]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 126 BPM, 4/4, A minor. Raw, pounding and physical: one riff and a drummer.

VOICE: Male, German, shouted and commanding with a lot of breath, like a gym instructor with a sense of humour. A gang shouts the chorus lines. The weekdays are whispered in the break.

INSTRUMENTS: A single buzzing analogue sequencer riff that never changes, a live drum kit hit hard with a simple four-on-the-floor pattern and open hi-hats, handclaps, nothing else until an alarm clock at the end.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, riff then drums. 0:14 Verse 1. 0:34 Chorus 1. 0:56 Verse 2. 1:16 Chorus 2. 1:38 Break, drums and whispered days. 1:58 Final chorus. 2:28 Outro, stop, a drum hit and an alarm at 2:52.

PRODUCTION & MIX: 1981 German new wave: brutally simple, dry and live, sequencer and drums in a bare room, voice loud.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first gang shout of 'Tanz den Montag!' at 0:34.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original cuts dictators down to dance steps. The tyrants in most people's lives now are the alarm, the calendar and the deadline, so those are the ones made to dance. Translation: dance the Monday, the calendar, the alarm clock, and clap your hands.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Ordered up, moving, laughing, sent home.
